question: A 53-year-old farmer presents to the clinic for evaluation of a pigmented lesion on his arm. He states that he first noticed the lesion last year, but he believes that it has been slowly growing in size. He otherwise does not have any complaints and is generally healthy. Which of the following findings on physical exam would suggest a malignant diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Asymmetry in pigmentation" -> "Irregular borders" -> "Varied colors within the lesion" -> "Possible malignant melanoma" -> 80% CHAIN: "Slowly growing lesion" -> "Irregular borders" -> "Varied pigmentation" -> "Suspicion for malignancy" -> 75% CHAIN: "Change in lesion size over time" -> "Irregular borders" -> "Varied pigmentation" -> "Concern for malignancy" -> 80%
analysis: The presence of different pigmentation throughout the lesion and the history of slow growth are concerning for malignancy. Asymmetry and changes in color are important features to consider in the evaluation of pigmented lesions.
